transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because my eating has just gotten all turned around lately. It's been going on for months now. Some days I just pick at a piece of toast and have some coffee, and that's all I can manage. But then other days, I'll find myself just standing in the bakery aisle buying all these sweets that I don't even really enjoy. It's just very off.
Over these past few months, have you noticed any significant change in your body weight—either up or down?

Well, it mostly just fluctuates. Like I was just saying, my eating has been all turned around for months now. Because I have those days where I only pick at toast and coffee, but then I have those other days where I'm buying all those bakery sweets... my weight just kind of goes up and down with it. I haven't noticed a huge drop or a big gain, it's just unstable because of how erratic my appetite has been.
During those times when you're eating a lot of sweets, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating, and does that leave you feeling distressed or guilty afterward?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel out of control or anything like I can't stop. It's more just... I buy them and eat them, but it's not some big frenzy. And I don't really feel guilty about it afterward, just maybe a little annoyed that my eating is so all over the place. But it doesn't cause me a lot of distress in that way.
Over these past few months, have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling persistently sad or down, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yes, I have. Well, most days I wake up with this heavy, sad feeling just sitting on me. It's hard to explain, but... even when I'm in my bright kitchen with the coffee going, I just feel like the warmth has gone out of everything.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it felt good at the time?

No, I haven't ever felt like that. I don't get bursts of energy or feel really high or anything. And I definitely don't feel like I need less sleep... if anything, I'm just tired a lot. So no, nothing like that.
Besides feeling sad, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, nearly every day for the past couple of weeks or more?

Yeah, I have. I used to get really excited about working on my quilting squares, or going out for bowling night. I was always the one planning the potlucks, too. But lately... I don't know, I just look at my sewing supplies or check the church calendar and I just can't make myself care the way I used to. The interest just isn't there anymore.
Have you had any thoughts of death, or felt like life isn't worth living, or had thoughts of harming yourself during this time?
No, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean, I feel sad and tired, but I don't want to die or hurt myself. I just want to feel like my normal self again.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to concentrate or make decisions, like trouble focusing on tasks or feeling more indecisive than usual, over these past couple of weeks?

No, I don't think so. I can still focus on things fine, like watching TV or reading. And making decisions hasn't been any harder than it usually is. I just don't have the energy or interest to do much, but my concentration seems okay.
Have you been feeling unusually worthless, or experiencing excessive guilt about things, during this period of feeling down?

No, not really. I don't feel worthless or anything like that. I mean, I feel bad that I haven't been helping out with the potlucks lately, but I wouldn't say it's excessive guilt. I just know I haven't been up to it. So, no, I don't think I've been feeling worthless or unusually guilty.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, such as trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

No, my sleep hasn't really changed. I still sleep about the same amount I always do. I don't have any trouble falling asleep at night, and I'm not sleeping the day away either. So, no, my sleep has been pretty normal.

You mentioned feeling this heavy, sad mood along with the loss of interest—how long, in total, have you been feeling this way? Has it been going on for just the past couple of weeks, or has it been present, even off and on, for two years or more?

It's been going on for about seven months now. It all started right around the time my aunt came to live with me, after she had a bad fall. So, yeah, it hasn't been two years, just the last seven months or so.
Over these past several months, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy nearly every day, even when you haven't been especially active?

Yes, I have been feeling pretty tired. Even after a full night of sleep, you know, on the nights when my aunt doesn't call out for me, I still feel completely worn down by the time I'm eating breakfast. It's just... little things, like carrying a basket of laundry or even just making a few phone calls, it all seems to take so much more out of me than it really should.

Have others noticed, or have you noticed yourself, that you've been moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or conversely feeling noticeably restless and unable to sit still, nearly every day during this time?

Yes, people have definitely noticed. Actually, people have started asking if my hip is bothering me again because I move so slow through the grocery store lately. And it's not just moving... I feel like it takes me forever to just answer a simple question when I'm talking to people. I'm just really slow right now.
